newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - India supports gasoline.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - India supports gasoline.

text.p: Emerging regional demand and the absorption of Chinese barrels propped up gasoline prices and widened the spread with lacklustre naphtha, traders said on Tuesday.
India has issued a tender for two more cargoes of February gasoline to Goa and Kandla on the west coast because of refinery maintenance.
Market sources told Reuters a 18,000 barrel-per-day fluid catalytic cracker at a Bombay refinery was due for a maintenance shutdown in February for thirty days.
The tenders seek 25,000 tonnes of 87-octane leaded gasoline for delivery on February 15-19 and February 21-25. They close January 22 and 29 respectively.
Taiwan also emerged with a tender to buy its March 1-15 requirement of 95-octane unleaded reformate. The tender closes Janaury 28.

Meanwhile, a Chinese refiner said it had already committed its February supplies last week of three to four 20-25,000-tonne cargoes of 93-octane at around $1.00 per barrel above Singapore naphtha spot quotes.
The seller said while it was too early to show March cargoes, the sharp fall in naphtha made naphtha-related sales unattractive.
Traders said some 95-octane cargoes in Singapore had been sold at $2.00 per barrel over naphtha quotes.
They said the spread between light distillates has widened as naphtha was comparatively weak amid an absence of buyers.

A U.S. major, previously targetting a premium of $1.00 per barrel over Singapore spot quotes, confirmed selling on Monday a 240,000 barrel cargo of light naphtha lifting in the first week of February at 80 cents per barrel to a Japanese end-user.
The seller said he was currently not showing his second cargo, for lifting late February.
Another Singapore refiner said cuts in throughputs would reduce its February availabilities by one cargo, but would not provide support to falling prices.
India's Madras tenders were heard awarded to a Japanese trader and a Dutch trader, but details could not be confirmed.
March naphtha swaps traded at $22.90.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
